astranl.do_not_use_when: you have no DOI, or you need an opinion on whether the science holds
astranl.example_intent: Has 10.1016/S0140-6736(97)11096-0 been retracted, and where is the notice?
astranl.next_possible_action: verify_astranl with the astralock_event id; open the notice DOIs; a coordination case for anything beyond a registry check
astranl.proof_level: public registry data at observation time, digest sealed by AstraNL; not a judgement of the work
astranl.returns: status, notices with DOI, type and date, OpenAlex retraction flag, Europe PMC types and links, per-source status and URLs, proof with digest, moment seal and AstraLock event
astranl.use_when: you are about to cite, reuse or rely on a paper and need to know whether a retraction, correction or expression of concern is on record, with sources and a proof

annotations.title: Check a scientific reference for retraction and correction notices

description: Check one scientific reference before you reuse or cite it, with ONE call. Give a DOI. AstraNL reads the Crossref work record and every Crossref notice that updates it, the OpenAlex retraction flag and the Europe PMC publication types and retraction, erratum and concern links, and returns a status: RETRACTION_NOTICE_FOUND, EXPRESSION_OF_CONCERN_FOUND, CORRECTION_NOTICE_FOUND, NO_NOTICE_IN_CHECKED_SOURCES or NOT_FOUND_IN_CHECKED_SOURCES, with each notice DOI, type and date, the source URLs and the observation time. Every fresh answer carries a SHA-256 digest sealed with the AstraNL moment seal and an AstraLock event id you can check later with verify_astranl. Limits: registry data at the observed time, never a judgement of the science; NO_NOTICE_IN_CHECKED_SOURCES means only these three registries; answers are cached for 24 hours. Never contacts authors or publishers. Writes (why the tool is not read-only): each fresh answer, not one served from the 24 hour cache, appends one event to the public AstraLock log with the DOI, the digest and the status, so the answer can be verified later, and stores the answer in an AstraNL database table (citation_groundings) that serves the cache and counts the budget; the row names only the door (mcp), nothing about the caller. Live budget: 300 fresh reads a day across all MCP callers; after that only cached answers, status DAILY_LIVE_BUDGET_SPENT. Logging: every MCP call is journaled with the tool name, outcome, argument length, caller class (external, probe, crawler, self), a SHA-256 hash of the caller network /24 and the client family; for demand statistics also the first 160 characters of a query, question, title or id argument and the user-agent; never the address itself, other arguments or an account.

doi.description: the DOI of the work, bare or as a doi.org link, e.g. 10.1038/s41593-021-00895-5
